ingredients.raw: 1 2-pound butternut squash, peeled, seeded and cut into 2-inch pieces (approximately 4 cups)
ingredients.preparation: peeled, seeded and cut into 2-inch pieces (approximately 4 cups)

ingredients.raw: 2 Northern Spy or McIntosh apples, peeled, cored and cut into 2-inch pieces (approximately 2 cups)
ingredients.preparation: peeled, cored and cut into 2-inch pieces (approximately 2 cups)

ingredients.raw: 1 large onion, peeled and coarsely chopped (approximately 1 cup)
¼ cup finely minced scallions, green tops included, for garnish

steps.text: Heat the peanut oil in a large stockpot over medium-low heat. Add the squash, apples and onion, stir to coat with oil and saute uncovered, stirring occasionally, for 10 to 15 minutes, or until the onion is transparent.
Stir in the mace, curry and cardamom and continue cooking until the onion begins to brown.

Add the cider. Bring the mixture to a boil over medium-high heat and cook for three minutes. Add the stock, lower the heat to medium-low and simmer the mixture, partially covered, for another 35 minutes, or until the squash is tender.

Transfer the mixture to a food-processor bowl and process until the soup is smooth, then return the soup to the stockpot. Reduce the soup, uncovered, over medium-low heat, to about one-fourth. Stir occasionally.
Stir in the half-and-half, salt and pepper and bring to a simmer. Pour into warmed bowls and sprinkle the scallions over the top.

name: Apple and Carrot Salad With Yogurt
author: Jacques Pépin

ingredients.raw: ¼ teaspoon freshly ground black pepper
4 carrots (12 ounces), peeled and shredded (3 ½ cups)
2 apples (12 ounces), left unpeeled but cored and cut into ¼-inch sticks (3 ½ cups)
ingredients.preparation: left unpeeled but cored and cut into ¼-inch sticks (3 ½ cups)

steps.text: Combine the yogurt, vinegar, pepper, salt and cilantro in a bowl. Add the carrots and apples, and mix well. Cover and refrigerate for a few hours to soften the carrots slightly.
Serve the salad with crusty bread or spoon it onto lettuce leaves.

name: Apple and Endive Salad With Grapefruit Dressing
author: Craig Claiborne

ingredients.raw: Salt and freshly ground black pepper
ingredients.item: salt and freshly ground black pepper

steps.text: To make the dressing whisk the mustard with the grapefruit juice, salt and pepper until mixture is light.
Whisk in oils until mixture is creamy.
Cut ends off the endive and wash well. Dry and cut in julienne strips.
Core but do not peel the apples. Cut in julienne strips. Mix apple with endive and cover immediately with dressing or apple will darken.
Serve on individual plates and sprinkle with mint leaves.

ingredients.raw: 1 extra-large egg yolk, at room temperature
½ cup crumbled Stilton or Gorgonzola cheese

steps.text: Combine the egg yolk, lemon juice and salt in a blender jar. Process on low speed just until blended. With the motor running on low speed, drizzle in the oil in a slow, steady stream. Fold in the honey and Calvados to taste.

Peel and core the apples, then cut them into small dice. Trim the ends off the celery and cut the stalks into small dice as well. Place both in a bowl with the walnuts. Spoon enough dressing over the mixture to coat all the components.

Trim the tough ends off the arugula. Wash the leaves well and dry in a salad spinner. Arrange them in a shallow salad bowl. Spoon the apple mixture into the center. Sprinkle the cheese around the edge.
Serve with the remaining dressing on the side.

ingredients.raw: 2 acorn squash, halved crosswise, seeds and fibers scooped out
ingredients.preparation: halved crosswise, seeds and fibers scooped out

ingredients.raw: 2 small McIntosh apples, halved, cored and cut into ¼-inch-thick slices
ingredients.preparation: halved, cored and cut into ¼-inch-thick slices

steps.text: Slice off the bottom of each squash half so that they stand flat, being careful not to cut into the flesh. Place in a medium-size roasting pan. Fan half of an apple in the cavity of each squash half. Add 1 teaspoon of butter and ¼ cup of the cider to each. Pour the remaining 2 cups of cider into the roasting pan. Cover the squash loosely with aluminum foil. Roast until the squash is tender, about 1 ½ hours. Place 1 squash half on each of 4 plates and serve immediately.

name: Apple Bear Claws
author: Vaughn Vreeland
description: Resembling something glorious between an almond croissant and a handheld fruit pie, these flaky pastries put an apple-y twist on bear claws. Classic ones use Danish dough to encase a frangipane filling made from finely ground almonds, and are shaped to resemble a bear’s paw. This version pays homage to the traditional, with frangipane in the center and apples that are cooked first so that they can start to soften, resulting in a firmer filling that’s easier to wrap. Store-bought puff pastry provides a ready-made stand-in for Danish pastry. Try to find a brand that is made with butter, such as Dufour, for optimal flavor. Make sure everything stays cold as you’re assembling the bear claws to prevent sticky dough — your refrigerator is your friend and your countertop will thank you.

ingredients.raw: 1 large apple, preferably Pink Lady or Honeycrisp
2 tablespoons/27 grams light or dark brown sugar
ingredients.item: tablespoons/27 grams light or dark brown sugar

ingredients.raw: 4 tablespoons/56 grams unsalted butter, melted and cooled
¼ cup/55 grams light brown sugar
1 (14- to 17-ounce) package frozen puff pastry, thawed
2 teaspoons milk, plus more as needed

steps.text: Core the apple (leaving it unpeeled) and cut into ½-inch cubes. In a medium saucepan over medium heat, melt the butter with the brown sugar, cinnamon and nutmeg, stirring. Once the mixture starts to bubble slowly, add the apple and salt, stirring to coat completely. Cook for 6 to 8 minutes, stirring often, until the apple has released a lot of its juices and has started to soften.

In a small bowl, stir together the cornstarch and lemon juice to make a slurry, then stir it into the apple mixture. After about a minute, the compote should look visibly thickened. Spread the compote in an even layer onto a plate or small baking sheet to cool quickly. Once it’s at room temperature, about 15 minutes, cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes (and up to a day).

In a medium bowl, mix together the almond flour, butter, brown sugar, almond extract and salt. Beat the egg in a small bowl with a fork until no streaks of egg white remain, then stir into the almond mixture. Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes (and up to a day).

Lightly flour a clean work surface, then unfold the puff pastry onto it and sprinkle the pastry with a bit more flour. If the puff pastry came as one sheet, cut it in half. Working one sheet at a time, roll each into a 10-by-12-inch rectangle, using more flour as needed. Cut each sheet of pastry into four 5-by-6-inch rectangles, rolling out more as needed. Place the 8 pieces of pastry on a large platter or baking sheet and refrigerate for a few minutes to relax the gluten and ensure they’re still cold.

In a small bowl, beat the egg white with a teaspoon of water until it’s slightly foamy. Line 2 baking sheets with parchment paper. (You’ll bake on two sheet pans, but only refrigerate one to save space.) Work with 4 pieces of pastry at a time, keeping the others refrigerated until ready to assemble.

Lay one of the pastry pieces lengthwise with the shorter edge closest to you. Spread a layer of the almond filling (a scant 2 tablespoons) on the half that’s nearest you and up to the center of the pastry, leaving a 1-inch border of pastry on the 3 remaining sides. Spread a layer of the apple filling on top (also a scant 2 tablespoons), then brush the egg white on the exposed border around the filling.

Fold the pastry over the filling, then crimp the edges with a lightly floured fork and cut 4 (½-inch) slits on the side closest to you with a paring knife. For the classic bear claw look, bring the folded corners of the uncut side toward each other to form a crescent. Place the pastry on one of the lined baking sheets and repeat with the remaining ingredients. Refrigerate the tray of shaped pastries for at least 30 minutes (and up to overnight) before baking; if refrigerating for more than 1 hour, cover the bear claws with plastic wrap, and cover and refrigerate the bowl of egg white as well.

When ready to bake, position oven racks in the upper and lower thirds of the oven and heat the oven to 375 degrees. Move 4 of the bear claws to the other lined baking sheet. Make sure the claws on both sheets are spaced at least 2 inches apart. Brush the tops of each pastry with the beaten egg white, then sprinkle with sliced almonds.

Bake for 25 to 35 minutes, switching the positions of the pans halfway through, until the bear claws are flaky, puffed and golden brown. Cool on the baking sheets for 10 minutes before transferring to a wire rack to cool for at least 10 more minutes so the filling can set before glazing.

In a small bowl, whisk together the powdered sugar and 2 teaspoons of milk. The glaze should be slightly runnier than honey; mix in a teaspoon more milk at a time if needed. Drizzle the glaze over the slightly cooled pastries, let it set for a couple minutes until dry, then enjoy. They’re best eaten day-of, either warm or at room temperature, but will keep in an airtight container for up to 3 days.

name: Apple, Cranberry and Goat Cheese Salad
author: Celia Barbour

ingredients.raw: ⅓ cup dried cranberries, chopped if desired
¼ cup extra virgin olive oil
1 tablespoon apple cider (or raspberry, pear or other fruity) vinegar
Finely grated zest of half an orange, optional
ingredients.item: finely grated zest of half an orange

ingredients.raw: Salt and freshly ground black pepper
ingredients.item: salt and freshly ground black pepper

ingredients.raw: 1 head lettuce, cored and torn into pieces, or mesclun mix
ingredients.preparation: cored and torn into pieces, or mesclun mix

steps.text: Preheat oven to 350 degrees. Toss pepitas with olive oil and salt in a bowl. Spread on baking sheet and toast in oven until golden and popped, 8 to 10 minutes. Remove and let cool. Place pepitas and cranberries in bottom of a salad bowl.
In another bowl, combine extra virgin olive oil, vinegar and zest, if using. Season to taste with salt and pepper. Whisk until emulsified.
Thinly slice each apple quarter crosswise, and add to salad bowl. Add lettuce and dressing, and toss to mix. Crumble cheese over salad and serve.

ingredients.raw: 1 small head romaine lettuce, broken into bite-size pieces
Salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste
ingredients.item: salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste

steps.text: Put 1 tablespoon of lemon juice in a bowl. Core and peel the apples, cut them into thin slices, and add them to the bowl, tossing gently to coat with lemon juice. Add romaine lettuce to the bowl, and toss gently again.
Combine the remaining 2 tablespoons of lemon juice with sugar, salt and pepper, and stir to blend. Add the oil, and beat to mix thoroughly. Taste the dressing, and adjust seasonings as desired.
Just before serving, add sardines to the apples, pour on the dressing, and toss the salad gently to coat all ingredients.

ingredients.raw: 2 tablespoons walnut oil or vegetable oil
Fresh ground black pepper to taste
ingredients.item: fresh ground black pepper to taste

steps.text: Wash and dry lettuce and break into bite-size pieces.
Wash and core apples and cut into cubes (do not peel).
Whisk together vinegar, oil and coriander in salad bowl. Add lettuce, apples and walnuts and toss. Season with pepper.

name: Apricot Thyme Chicken and Chickpeas
author: Nargisse Benkabbou
description: Inspired by the sweet-and-savory balance found in Moroccan tagines, this vibrant sheet-pan dinner delivers bold, layered flavor with minimal effort. At the heart of the dish is a glossy marinade built around apricot jam, which adds a gentle fruitiness and helps keep the chicken tender and juicy as it roasts. The jam is mixed with garlic, thyme, soy sauce and warm spices like turmeric and ginger, creating a rich sauce that flavors both the chicken and the vegetables. As the chicken cooks, a bed of onions and chickpeas soaks up its juices, becoming soft and caramelized. Green olives, added toward the end, bring a brininess that adds contrast. Serve with your choice of sides, such as couscous, rice or flatbread.

ingredients.raw: 2 ½ to 3 pounds bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs (about 7 chicken thighs)
½ cup vegetable or chicken stock
2 tablespoons chopped thyme, plus more for garnish if desired
ingredients.preparation: plus more for garnish if desired

ingredients.raw: ½ cup pitted green olives (such as Castelvetrano)
Couscous, rice or flatbread, for serving

steps.text: Heat the oven to 400 degrees. Add the chicken thighs to a large bowl and season them on both sides with ¾ teaspoon salt.

Make the marinade: In a medium bowl, combine the vegetable stock, apricot jam, olive oil, soy sauce, thyme, garlic, turmeric, ginger and ¾ teaspoon salt. Pour about half of the marinade over the chicken and turn to coat.

On a sheet pan, combine the onions, chickpeas and remaining marinade and toss to coat. Arrange the onions and chickpeas in a single layer and place the chicken on top, skin side up. Roast for 30 minutes, until the chicken starts to brown.
Remove the pan from the oven, scatter the olives around the chicken and roast for 10 to 15 minutes more, until the chicken is cooked through and golden, and the onions are soft and caramelized.
Garnish with thyme if desired and serve immediately.
